This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Wuhan Tianhe International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Wuhan Tianhe International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/wuhan/ZHHH.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from sources including AccuWeather, BBC Weather, and timeanddate.com indicate a daily maximum near 34–35 °C in Wuhan on August 19, 2026, under partly cloudy to overcast skies with isolated thundershowers possible in the afternoon. These conditions align with Wuhan’s subtropical monsoon climate, where August averages hover around 32 °C but can reach the mid-30s amid high humidity and light northeasterly winds. Recent model consensus shows limited intensification potential, keeping 35 °C as the leading outcome at 48.5 % implied probability while 36 °C trails at 36.0 %. Afternoon observations and any revisions to steering patterns or convective timing remain the key variables that could shift the final recorded high within the narrow 34–37 °C range dominating market sentiment.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model runs project a Seattle high near 77°F on August 19, 2026, positioning the 76–79°F bands as the clear market leaders with over 70% combined implied probability. Persistent onshore flow off the Pacific maintains a moderating marine layer that caps daytime warming, while weak upper-level ridging provides limited support for reaching the upper 70s rather than pushing into the 80s. Recent forecast updates show minimal spread across guidance, reflecting stable synoptic conditions and typical late-August climatology for the region, where marine influences frequently keep maxima in this narrow range. Updated model runs and afternoon observations will provide the final inputs for resolution.

Recent model guidance shows no major anomalies or strong disturbances expected for August 20, keeping the distribution centered on 31–33°C while reflecting high day-to-day variability from localized showers. Key variables include the timing and intensity of convective rainfall—earlier or heavier storms favor outcomes near 30°C or below by limiting peak heating—along with wind patterns that influence boundary-layer mixing and humidity. Clearer conditions or delayed convection could push readings to 34°C or higher, though historical data indicate such peaks remain infrequent amid persistent moisture and high relative humidity near 80%. Official forecasts from agencies like Panama's ETESA will provide critical updates on these factors ahead of market resolution.
